full_judgment:
5. The suit of the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 was dismissed and the suit of the present appellant and others was decreed. As against the judgments of the trial court respondent Nos. 3 and 4 filed Other Appeal Nos. 31 and 30 of 1994 respectively before the court of District Judge, Chittagong and both the appeals were dismissed. The respondent Nos.3 and 4 moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained a Rule being Civil Revision No. 1207 of 1999 against the judgment and decree passed in Other Appeal No. 30 of 1994 and also obtained an order of stay for a period of 6(six) months. The respondent Nos. 3 and 4 also filed Civil Revision No. 1259 of 1999 against the judgment and decree in Other Appeal No. 31 of 1994 and obtained an order of stay for a period of 6 months. 

 11. From the photocopy of the daily cause list dated 05.11.2000 it appears that the writ petition No. 2999 of 1999 was posted in the daily cause list at serial No. 11 of the Bench for hearing two applications. From the cause list of the same Bench dated 06.11.2000 it appears that the writ petition at serial number 3 was posted for order but instead of disposing of the applications the main Rule was discharged. Thus it is clear that the writ petition (Rule) was not posted for hearing in the daily cause list of the Bench rather two applications filed in the writ petition were listed for hearing and while disposing of the applications the Rule itself was discharged without hearing the parties. This is a patent illegality committed by the High Court Division. Annexure-D is a copy of application filed by the respondent No. 3 to the Waqf Administrator requesting him to take action in the matter of management of the Waqf Estate in the light of the order dated 26.04.1999 passed by the High Court Division in the Civil Revision. The High Court Division on 26.04.1999 issued Rule in Civil Revision No. 1207 of 1999 and also stayed the judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal for a period of 6 months. On the basis of this prayer of the respondent No. 3, respondent No. 1 passed the order dated 22.07.1999 stating that in the light of the order of the High Court Division dated 26.04.1999 the Waqf Estate shall be managed by Respondent No. 3. 

 12. We have already indicated that by the order dated 26.04.1999 passed in Civil Revision No. 1207 of 1999 the High Court Division simply issued Rule and stayed operation of the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court and no other order was passed.
